papers.title: First Order Geometry of Equilateral Small Polygons
papers.abstract: We develop a first order calculus based on the geometry of realised diameter graphs for perimeter maximisation among convex equilateral small polygons. Polygon side equalities and active diameter constraints define a linearised feasible cone and an associated equality space. We prove that an equilateral small polygon is a strict local maximiser of perimeter modulo Euclidean motions if a multiplier balance holds with strictly positive active diameter multipliers and the active equality space consists only of infinitesimal Euclidean motions. The proof uses a local Euclidean slice and a geometric limiting argument and requires neither independence of the active constraint gradients nor second order information. As an application, we combine our criterion with validated interval arithmetic to establish strict local maximality for Bingane and Audet's polygons $A_{16}$, $A_{32}$, $A_{64}$ and for reconstructions of their polygons $Z_{32}$ and $Z_{64}$. For each $n\in\{32,64\}$, the perimeter of $Z_n$ is strictly larger than that of $A_n$. Thus, strict local maximisers with different perimeters coexist in the space of convex equilateral small polygons with the same number of sides.

papers.title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
papers.abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for two parameters, $n,m\ge2$ and an uncountable field, a class containing such a family admits no coarse embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance, on the space of rank invariants, the asymptotic dimension and the Assouad-Nagata dimension are again $2(n+m)$: slope-one slices pin the grid of grades, and over a grid only finitely many rank invariants occur; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

papers.title: Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls: a survey
papers.abstract: What is the largest constant $c\in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of axis-parallel squares in the plane admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $c$ of the area covered by $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T.~Rad\'o in 1928, who was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. R.~Rado later generalized the problem from axis-parallel squares in the plane to homothetic copies of any given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where now we are looking for an optimal constant $F(K)$. In this paper we survey the literature on this problem, with a focus on the case where $K$ is a cube or a ball in the high-dimensional regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. The estimates that we currently have for cubes are much more precise than those for balls: namely if $Q^d$ is a $d$-dimensional cube, then \[ (e^{-1}+o(1))\frac{2^{-d}}{d \log{d}} \leq F(Q^d)\leq 2^{-d}, \] while denoting $B^d$ a $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball, then \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq F(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}.\] Except for the upper bound for cubes, which is classical, the other estimates are due to the authors.

papers.title: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension
papers.abstract: In this work, we formalize the concept of intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes introduced in Li et al. (2018), which measures the structural complexity of learning problems by training along randomly generated subspaces. We define the intrinsic dimension of a set $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ as the minimal dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ such that a random plane of dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ in $\mathbb{R}^p$ intersects $\Theta$ with probability one. We show that it is a generalized notion of co-dimension that depends on the global geometry of $\Theta$. We study mathematical properties of the intrinsic dimension and develop techniques to estimate the intrinsic dimension of sets $\Theta$ that arise in learning problems. More specifically, we derive upper and/or lower bounds where $\Theta$ is the set of optimal parameters in student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks, including finite and infinite sample cases, and with and without regularization. We discuss how our theory leads to novel types of generalization bounds, thereby showing that the intrinsic dimension is a measure of learning complexity. Our results connect techniques from seemingly different areas of machine learning research such as classification of symmetries of ReLU networks and stochastic geometry.

papers.title: A Sharp Perimeter Inequality for Mean Distances on Convex Curves
papers.abstract: For a planar convex body $K$, let $\theta(K)$ denote the expected Euclidean distance between two independent points uniformly distributed on $\partial K$ with respect to arclength. We prove the sharp inequality $$\frac{\theta(K)}{\operatorname{per}K}>\frac{1}{6}.$$ The constant is approached by rectangles degenerating to a segment.

papers.title: Continuous improved H\"{o}lder and reverse H\"{o}lder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
papers.abstract: We establish continuous versions of the improved H\"{o}lder and reverse H\"{o}lder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

papers.title: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
papers.abstract: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. For every $d \geq 4$, we construct $\lceil\frac{(d-1)^2}{2}\rceil$ sets in $\mathbb R^d$ whose geometric join is not contractible, disproving the conjecture of B\'ar\'any, Holmsen, and Karasev that the geometric join of at least $d+1$ sets is contractible.

papers.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I \gamma_{\Sigma_i}(K_i)^{\tilde \lambda_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}\gamma_\Gamma\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,\Sigma_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $\gamma_{\Sigma_i}$ is zero, where $\lambda_i, \tilde \lambda_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde \lambda_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $\Gamma, \Sigma_1,\cdots,\Sigma_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I \lambda_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} \gamma_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

papers.title: Banchoff Curvature and Realisation Moduli of Piecewise-Affine Arrangement Immersions
papers.abstract: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-M\"uller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.

papers.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties. We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{\chi_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.

papers.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

papers.title: A Universal $8$-Vertex Origami Torus Triangulation
papers.abstract: An origami torus is a piecewise affine isometric embedding of a flat torus into $\R^3$. We prove that every flat torus is realized as an $8$-vertex origami torus based on the triangulation with degree sequence $4,6,6,6,6,6,7,7$. This provides an $8$-vertex universal triangulation for origami tori.

papers.title: Three Circles in a Unit Disk: Three Solutions to an Extremal Problem
papers.abstract: We place two disks inside the unit disk so that they touch each other and the unit circle. We then insert a disk of the largest possible radius, requiring it to touch both original disks. We show that the smallest possible sum of the three areas is $11\pi/18$, and find all equality cases. We give three solutions, using Descartes' circle theorem, inversion, and contact-point coordinates. The main difficulty is checking that the third disk is largest among all disks that fit, not only among disks touching the first two.

papers.title: On the volume growth assumption in the Eulerian definition of RCD spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinitesimally Hilbertian metric measure space whose reference measure is a Radon measure, and which satisfies the Sobolev-to-Lipschitz property and the weak Bochner inequality with a lower Ricci bound, has Gaussian volume growth; in particular, balls have finite measure. Hence, in the Eulerian definition of $\mathsf{RCD}(K,\infty)$ spaces, both the volume growth assumption and the finiteness of the measure of balls are redundant. The proof combines the self-improvement of the Bakry--\'Emery gradient estimate, obtained without using the conservation of mass of the heat flow, with a dimension-free Harnack inequality derived from the Sobolev-to-Lipschitz property.

papers.title: Liouville regular Jordan curves
papers.abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.

papers.title: Contractibility of the Gromov--Hausdorff cloud of a Hilbert space
papers.abstract: The cloud of a metric space $X$ consists of all metric spaces at finite Gromov--Hausdorff distance from $X$, with spaces at zero distance identified. We prove that the cloud of every real Hilbert space $H$ admits a strong deformation retraction onto the point represented by $H$.

papers.title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le \alpha<1$, we construct a $C^{1,\alpha}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. In step-2 Carnot groups, we show that every $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension less than or equal to $q-\frac{1+\alpha}2$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. This upper bound is actually attained by the $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces of our construction, hence their Euclidean Hausdorff dimension is maximal. As a technical result of independent interest, we show that the implicit function associated with a $C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurface is $\frac{1+\alpha}2$-Euclidean H\"older continuous, with $0\le\alpha\le 1$. In particular, $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm H}$ hypersurfaces in step-2 Carnot groups are rectifiable in the classical sense, therefore the range of unrectifiability $0\le \alpha<1$ is sharp. We also prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. The previous results extend the seminal work of Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group and settle a question concerning the singular surface they constructed, by proving that its $\frac52$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure is zero.
